title: Rhetorical methods card
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Writing to argue and persuade; end of year
source: Written for english/y8 lesson 73 (Rhetorical methods card (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 73: HEMPS: choosing rhetorical methods for effect. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Method
Example
rows: Who chose the last leader you followed?
We deserve a voice. We deserve a choice. We deserve a say.

model.title: Upgrade: Pupils should have a say in who leads them.

parts.text: Inclusive pronoun: We should have a say...
Anaphora: We deserve a voice. We deserve a choice.
Rhetorical question: Why should leadership be decided for us?
Check: does each method serve the point?

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: We deserve a voice. We deserve a choice. Why should leadership be decided for us, and not by us?

head: Not this
This
rows: Is it not absolutely, totally, completely the most important issue in the entire history of the universe?!
This is the most important decision we will make this year.

keywords.def: the school's frame for selecting and applying effective rhetorical methods
words chosen to make the audience feel strongly
repeating words at the start of sentences for effect

questions.q: Add anaphora to: Leaders should listen. Leaders should explain.
questions.a: For example: A good leader listens. A good leader explains. A good leader serves.

questions.q: Core: add three rhetorical methods to your speech and label them in the margin
Extend: write a note explaining why each method suits your audience
Stretch: remove one method that is decoration rather than argument
questions.a: One method removed with a reason

questions.q: When is a rhetorical method most effective?
options: when it strengthens a clear point
when it hides a weak argument
questions.a: A) when it strengthens a clear point. Methods should serve the argument; overuse weakens it.
C) repetition at the start of sentences
options: repetition at the start of sentences
